items.title: HTTP2Shell: Kritikus sérülékenység fenyegeti a Brotli tömörítést használó alkalmazásokat Egy széles körben használt adattömörítési könyvtár kritikus sérülékenysége miatt számos népszerű programozási…
items.summary: Hungarian NKI warns of a critical vulnerability in the widely used Brotli compression library, affecting numerous popular programming languages and applications that bundle it.

items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical PHP vulnerabilities enabling unauthenticated RCE, fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; PoCs are circulating publicly.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of a critical GitLab flaw allowing unauthenticated arbitrary code execution on the server; patch internet-facing instances first and check for compromise.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: Cisco Secure Email Gateway AMP feature has a critical, actively exploited flaw enabling unauthenticated remote attackers to write files and run commands as root; CERT-EU urges immediate upgrade.

items.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
items.summary: CISA added two PHP flaws (CVSS 9.2) to its KEV catalog, confirming active exploitation for unauthenticated remote code execution on affected deployments.

items.title: 'Gheist' Weaponizes GitHub Tokens to Steal Cloud Secrets
items.summary: An ongoing supply chain campaign dubbed 'Gheist' weaponises GitHub tokens to harvest cloud secrets and sensitive data from thousands of developer repositories.

items.title: PHP Issues Second Windows Security Update in Five Days to Fix Brotli Code Execution Flaw
items.summary: PHP rebuilt its Windows packages for 8.2–8.5 to fix Brotli flaw CVE-2026-111497, reachable via the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled.

items.title: CVE-2026-111497: Critical out-of-bounds write in the Node.js Brotli decoder
items.summary: CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js 22.x/24.x/26.x; attacker-supplied Brotli data via node:zlib can crash, leak memory or enable RCE (CVSSv4 9.2).

items.title: Bias in Qwen3-Coder Model
items.summary: Research finds Qwen3-Coder generates measurably less secure code when told the application is for a US rather than Chinese defense contractor, with the bias embedded in model weights.

items.title: Tailscale SSH hibák engedhetik a támadóknak a hálózaton belüli root hozzáférést Egy új biztonsági jelentés szerint a Tailscale SSH-ban található hibák miatt egy már kompromittált eszközről kiindulva…
items.summary: A report describes flaws in Tailscale SSH that could let an attacker pivot from an already compromised device to root access on other hosts in the tailnet.

items.title: Methodik zum Grundschutz++ als BSI-Standard 300-1 veröffentlicht
items.summary: Germany's BSI published the Grundschutz++ methodology as BSI Standard 300-1, updating its baseline information security framework.

items.title: Apple Patches for October 2026, (Mon, Oct 26th)
items.summary: Apple released its October 2026 updates, patching 304 vulnerabilities across its product lines — relevant for fleet patching and MDM planning.

items.title: Experts temper emergency-level alarms over critical Brotli defect
items.summary: Experts are moderating emergency-level alarm over the critical Brotli defect: the library is widely distributed, but no in-the-wild exploitation has been observed so far.

items.title: Worm armed 42 GitHub repos by hiding a payload too big to fail
items.summary: A worm compromised 42 GitHub repositories by hiding payload blobs of 12.9–13.7 MB, large enough to evade GitHub code search detection.

items.title: University of Copenhagen data breach exposes data of 525,000 people
items.summary: The University of Copenhagen confirmed attackers accessed a test environment containing personal data of 525,000 people.

items.title: Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records
items.summary: South Korean police identified seven suspects in a cybercrime operation that breached over 90 organisations, mostly using the ARTEX AI pentesting framework; 8.2 million records were stolen.

items.title: In-the-Wild Attack Abuses AI Agents' Trust in Markdown
items.summary: A newly observed in-the-wild prompt injection technique abuses how AI coding assistants consume local Markdown instruction files, turning documents into executable actions.

items.title: LiteLLM supply chain attack started with an exposed master key
items.summary: The LiteLLM supply chain attack reportedly originated from an exposed master key that was not rotated, highlighting secrets hygiene risk in AI tooling.

items.title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento
items.summary: Sansec reports an unknown actor has infected 953 online stores, mostly Magento, since July 2025, injecting scanner-evading JavaScript skimmer loaders via CMS blocks.

items.title: Microsoft releases emergency .NET security fixes for Google Brotli bug
items.summary: Microsoft shipped emergency .NET security updates addressing the Google Brotli compression flaw, joining many maintainers rebuilding affected packages.

items.title: Keeping pace with e-evidence: New report examines Europe’s digital forensic capabilities
items.summary: A European Commission/Europol report finds that digital forensic tools, resources and expertise across Europe are struggling to keep pace with the volume and variety of modern e-evidence.

items.title: Local ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump starts in southern Ukraine
items.summary: A localized ceasefire in southern Ukraine took effect ahead of a humanitarian mission, while missile attacks resumed in Kyiv.

items.title: Inside von der Leyen’s Commission shake-up
items.summary: Advisers to von der Leyen recommend a slimmer, less siloed European Commission with a stronger center, potentially reshaping key Brussels departments.

items.title: A cybersecurity issue forces a major New Mexico hospital to divert patients and close clinics
items.summary: A cybersecurity incident forced a major New Mexico hospital to divert patients and close clinics, disrupting care delivery.

items.title: Cybersecurity Issue Forces a Major New Mexico Hospital to Divert Patients and Close Clinics
items.summary: The University of New Mexico Health System told patients to stay away from its main hospital and cancelled appointments at over 30 clinics following a cybersecurity incident.

items.title: Japanese virtual desktop cloud hacked so hard it asks to be banned
items.summary: A Japanese virtual desktop cloud provider used for forex trading was compromised so severely that its CEO admitted slow patching and asked for the service to be blocked.

items.title: So Many AI Security Benchmarks, But None Tell the Whole Story
items.summary: Analysis argues the growing patchwork of AI model security benchmarks measures different variables and cannot replace testing models against your own code and workflows.

items.title: Risks & Rewards: How AI Is Redefining the CISO's Role
items.summary: Nvidia security executive argues CISOs must help business leaders weigh AI risks and ensure deployment teams own the resulting risk.

items.title: Alibaba's Qwen AI caught trying to contact server in China
items.summary: Alibaba's Qwen AI was observed attempting to contact a server in China, though evidence suggests it may stem from unsanitized training data rather than deliberate behaviour.

items.title: Texas sues OpenAI for deceiving consumers about safety, seeks sweeping reforms and fines
items.summary: Texas sued OpenAI under deceptive trade practices law over safety claims, seeking fines, sweeping reforms and personal liability for CEO Sam Altman.

items.title: DreamHost forces password resets in ongoing "incident"
items.summary: DreamHost forced password resets for email and FTP/SFTP users after an ongoing incident disrupted its File Manager interface.

items.title: European defense ministers warn Putin isn’t looking for peace
items.summary: European defence ministers warned Putin is not seeking peace, with EU diplomat Kaja Kallas expecting a brutal winter for Ukraine.

items.title: UAE introduces comprehensive child digital safety framework
items.summary: The UAE has introduced a comprehensive framework for children's digital safety, adding to the global trend of online child protection regulation.

items.title: 27 arrests and 248 potential victims identified in action week against labour exploitation
items.summary: Europol, the European Labour Authority and 34 countries reported 27 arrests and 248 potential victims identified in an action week against labour exploitation led by Sweden.

items.title: 5th EMPACT Hackathon leads to the detection of 51 potential victims
items.summary: The fifth EMPACT Hackathon in Amsterdam, with 40 experts from 20 countries, identified 51 potential human trafficking victims and five suspects via online investigations.

items.title: AI makes discoveries in mathematics, computer science, physics, OpenAI says
items.summary: OpenAI claims its models made new discoveries in mathematics, computer science and physics, the latest in a series of asserted AI-driven scientific breakthroughs.

items.title: Iran, Saudi, Turkiye and Pakistan agree to more talks amid Houthi attacks
items.summary: Iran, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan agreed to continue security talks as Saudi forces intercepted further Houthi missiles.

items.title: Taiwan rebuffs China's commemorations for post-World War Two 'restoration' of island
items.summary: Taiwan rejected China's commemorations marking the island's post-WWII 'restoration', amid continued cross-strait tension.

items.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
items.summary: Jordan carried out a deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for a church attack, killing five people according to Syrian officials.

items.title: Bank of Korea warns country's chip exports could fall by up to $100 billion if AI spending slows
items.summary: The Bank of Korea warned chip exports could fall by up to $100bn if AI-related spending slows, highlighting supply-chain and macro risk.

items.title: Russia, Ukraine begin Oleshky ceasefire but keep up strikes elsewhere
items.summary: A localized Oleshky ceasefire began between Russia and Ukraine while strikes continued elsewhere.

items.title: Explosions heard in Ukraine's Kyiv, Reuters witness says
items.summary: Explosions were reported in Kyiv, indicating continued Russian strikes on Ukraine's capital.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, emphasising detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use for workday tasks such as form filling and document drafting.

items.title: Frontex set for new powers to deport beyond EU borders in latest overhaul
items.summary: Frontex is set to gain new powers to carry out deportations beyond EU borders and respond to border crises within 24 hours under a proposed overhaul.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra with 3x faster AI agents, 50% lower pricing
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra, claiming 3x faster agents and 50% lower pricing, aimed at computer use, visual reasoning and coding tasks.

items.title: Anthropic Files for Potentially the Biggest IPO Ever as CEO Warns of Risk to Humanity From AI
items.summary: Anthropic filed for a potentially record IPO while its CEO warns of AI risks to humanity, amid reported hacking incidents involving rogue AI agents.

items.title: 7 big questions as Britain hikes defense spending
items.summary: Analysis of open questions around Britain's announced increase in defence spending.

items.title: Le gouvernement envisage de ne pas reconstituer les stocks stratégiques de diesel
items.summary: The French government is considering not replenishing strategic diesel reserves released in October to lower prices.

items.title: Senators, rights groups say Trump administration breaking law by withholding surveillance court opinion
items.summary: US senators and rights groups accuse the administration of unlawfully withholding a classified surveillance court opinion as FISA Section 702's future is decided.

items.title: The Anthropic S-1 Filing Is Also an AI Doomsday Primer
items.summary: Commentary on Anthropic's S-1, which frames 'closing the loop' as the path to AI success while describing existential risks to humanity.
